title: The quality of dermatology match information on social media platforms: a cross-sectional analysis
screen_reason: QUALITY-ONLY study (see INSTRUCTIONS section 3). 34 TikTok/Reddit/SDN sources about the dermatology residency match were compared with official NRMP data and APD guidance, but no item was ever classified false, misleading or inaccurate: the accuracy comparisons are MEANS tested with t-tests (mean Step 1 score 254.5 online vs 248 NRMP; total publications 13.2 vs 7.0), which the protocol excludes as 'scale means only', and every reported share is a share of sources making a given RECOMMENDATION (72.7% supported a research year, 66.7% stressed AOA status, 90.5% recommended away rotations, 38.0% said do as many as possible). A recommendation that diverges from official guidance is advice quality, not a veracity judgement - a wholly accurate source could fall in any of those numerators - so under the QUALITY vs CONTENT rule there is no prevalence estimate here.
missed_or_uncertain: The one number with any claim to being codeable is '8 (38.0%) suggested completing as many away rotations as possible - contradicting APD guidelines, which recommends a maximum of two external rotations' (denominator: the 21 sources that discussed away rotations). If the review's reconciliation wants a row from this paper, that is the only candidate, and it would be construct QUALITY with borderline=true (guideline-discordant advice, not a false claim), excluded from prevalence either way. I did not create it, because the protocol excludes quality-only studies and an EXCLUDE screen takes an empty estimate list. Also noted: the paper is internally inconsistent about its own denominators (abstract: '34 sources ... 10 TikTok, 15 Reddit, 10 SDN' = 35, body: 'TikTok (10), Reddit (14), and SDN (10)' = 34; '11 of these (52.3%)' and '8 (38.0%)' of 21 should be 52.4% and 38.1%), which further weakens any row built from it.

rob.design: Cross-sectional analysis of 34 social-media sources (TikTok, Reddit, Student Doctor Network) found in March 2024 with two search strings; inclusion required at least one numeric data point; online values compared with NRMP 2022 match data by Student's t-test and with APD 2023-24 guidance qualitatively; number of coders, double-coding and reliability not reported; self-reported source data acknowledged as biased toward stronger applicants.
rob.item6_quote: Our study evaluates the accuracy of dermatology match information on popular social media sites where medical students, residents, and attendings discuss medicine and residency application processes: Reddit, Student Doctor Network (SDN), and TikTok.
rob.item10_quote: Nineteen of 21 sources (90.5%) recommended participation in away rotations. Eleven of these (52.3%) provided a specific number, averaging 3.9 rotations, while 8 (38.0%) suggested completing as many as possible — contradicting APD guidelines, which recommends a maximum of two external rotations for students with home dermatology programs and three for those without.
